transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Ava Patel (Redwood CSM); Diane Morales (Bridgewell Procurement), Raj Patel (Bridgewell CISO), Lena Ortiz (Bridgewell MLOps), Tom Nguyen (Bridgewell Legal)

Summary:
Quick procurement and legal review covering MSA/DPA comments, SLA expectations, pricing tiers for Dedicated vs Hosted, and next steps for pilot/benchmarks. Bridgewell flagged three areas: data residency, KMS/encryption, and uptime/penalty language in SLAs. Redwood AE committed to pricing and capacity worksheet; SE to share benchmark test plan.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and timeline
- DPA clauses (data retention, deletion, subprocessors)
- SLA targets and credit/penalty language
- Pricing: hosted per-token vs Dedicated committed capacity
- Onboarding & pilot: test plan, timelines, telemetry

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account. Marcus our solutions engineer is here, and Ava from customer success.
[00:06] Diane Morales: Hi, thanks Sofia. Diane here. We booked this to go through the MSA and DPA redlines and make sure SLAs and pricing align with legal and procurement.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Raj, CISO. I'll focus on security, encryption, key management and subprocessor list.
[00:16] Lena Ortiz: Lena from MLOps, want to talk pilot benchmarks and any constraints for private deployment.
[00:21] Marcus Lee: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines, 2) SLAs and uptime/credits, 3) pricing models for hosted vs dedicated, 4) next steps for pilot. Sound good?
[00:28] Tom Nguyen: Sounds fine. I already sent a few redlines to Sofia in email but want to walk through the biggest ones.
[00:33] Sofia Chen: Perfect, Tom — we got them. I'll run through our standard positions and note where we can be flexible. First, MSA term and termination: your request for unlimited liability carve-outs for data breaches — can you highlight which sections you need adjusted?
[00:46] Tom Nguyen: Sure, section 9.2 and 12. We need a clearer cap for damages, and also specific language around indemnification related to data processed for regulatory obligations.
[00:58] Marcus Lee: From a technical standpoint, on indemnity we can accept language tied to Redwood's willful misconduct, but standard carve-outs for third-party data processors are tricky — we do have SOC 2 and ISO reports we can provide.
[01:14] Raj Patel: On SOC2/ISO — can you share the latest reports and any penetration test summaries? Also details on your KMS: customer-managed keys support?
[01:23] Marcus Lee: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated in certain regions. For hosted API customers, we offer envelope encryption and can work with a managed KMS arrangement; full HSM integration is available as an enterprise add-on. We'll attach the security pack.
[01:36] Diane Morales: OK that helps. For DPA: we need explicit subprocessors list and a deletion confirmation window — 30 days maximum after termination.
[01:45] Sofia Chen: The subprocessors list is published and maintained; we'll share the current list and a process for notification. Regarding retention and deletion, our standard is 60 days for backups, but operationally we can agree to a 30- or 45-day window in the DPA for Bridgewell if it's a contractual requirement — need to confirm with infra ops though.
[02:03] Tom Nguyen: 60 days is a hard stop for us, 30 is preferred. Can you confirm immutable backups policy?
[02:10] Marcus Lee: Immutable backups are handled by the cloud provider layer; we can document the retention and deletion flow, including how cached KV entries are cleaned up. For Private deployments, customer controls retention fully.
[02:22] Lena Ortiz: On the deployment side, we are evaluating two flows: hosted API for early dev and a Dedicated pool or VPC private deployment for PHI workload. Need to understand SLA differences and pricing delta.
[02:33] Sofia Chen: Sure — hosted API is easiest to start, pay-as-you-go per-token. Dedicated and Private are committed capacity with monthly/annual commits, much lower per-token unit economics and predictable throughput. Our Dedicated offering comes with better latency SLOs and dedicated GPU pools.
[02:48] Diane Morales: What are typical SLA numbers and credit mechanics? Our procurement needs minimum 99.9% monthly uptime with credits tiered by minutes under.
[02:56] Marcus Lee: Our standard SLA for Dedicated is 99.95% with defined credits. Hosted tiers vary by plan; we can provide sample SLA language. The big thing is the definition of downtime — we usually exclude scheduled maintenance with notice and force majeure. We can discuss making scheduled maintenance windows narrower for committed contracts.
[03:14] Raj Patel: We also need clarity on how fallbacks work — if Dedicated capacity is unavailable, do you route to hosted models? That has data residency implications.
[03:23] Sofia Chen: Good point. We have smart routing policies: you can configure failover to compatible model variants in the same region or to a hosted fallback. For Bridgewell, we can lock routing to within a region or to Dedicated-only, and disable hosted fallback if data residency forbids it. We'll note that in the config.
[03:39] Tom Nguyen: Regarding SLAs and penalties — can you accept a carve-out that allows us to withhold payment or get higher credits if SLOs fall below target more than twice in a quarter?
[03:49] Marcus Lee: We typically negotiate credit thresholds; withholding payment is harder, but additional credits and remediation commitments can be added for severe regressions.
[03:57] Diane Morales: On pricing — what's the delta between hosted and Dedicated for our expected volumes? We estimate ~50M tokens/month initially, growing to 200M in 12 months.
[04:08] Sofia Chen: For 50M tokens/month, hosted per-token pricing is higher; Dedicated committed capacity reduces unit cost by ~40-60% depending on model and quantization. We'll run a committed capacity worksheet with three scenarios: baseline hosted, small dedicated commit, and full reserved.
[04:23] Lena Ortiz: Important for us: benchmarking latency at 2k token context for our summarization pipeline. Will Redwood run an initial bench or do we run it?
[04:33] Marcus Lee: We can run an initial benchmark in our lab with a representative prompt set, then mirror it in your environment for Dedicated or Private. For the pilot, we recommend Redwood-run baseline + customer-run verification. We'll define test vectors, concurrency profile, and expected latencies.
[04:48] Tom Nguyen: Legal question — subprocessors list changes: we need notification 30 days prior to adding a subprocessor. Is that feasible?
[04:55] Sofia Chen: Yes, we can commit to notify customers 30 days in advance for new subprocessors with opt-out rights for major changes.
[05:04] Raj Patel: Encryption in transit and at rest — TLS for transit is standard. For at-rest, we need AES-256 and customer-managed KMS for PHI. Also need key rotation policies and proof of zero access.
[05:14] Marcus Lee: Agreed. We support AES-256; customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated in supported regions. For hosted we have envelope encryption and can discuss HSM solutions. We'll provide the key rotation and access control doc.
[05:27] Diane Morales: Can you share SOC 2 type II and ISO certs? Also privacy whitepaper and subprocessor list.
[05:32] Sofia Chen: Yes, we'll attach the security pack and add a slide with the current subprocessors list.
[05:37] Lena Ortiz: For pilot timing — we want a two-week pilot to validate latency and accuracy, followed by a 30-day POC for throughput. Is that something you typically do?
[05:46] Sofia Chen: Yes, a 2-week technical pilot (benchmarks + telemetry), then a 30-day POC for broader testing. For Dedicated we can offer a short-term burst capacity to support the POC.
[05:55] Tom Nguyen: On indemnity and data breach notice periods — we asked for 48-hour notification for confirmed breaches. Can you do that?
[06:02] Marcus Lee: 48 hours is tight, but for confirmed incidents we commit to immediate notification; we typically aim for 72 hours for initial notification if there's investigation required. We'll flag this as a negotiation point.
[06:12] Raj Patel: We need a runbook for incident response and a contact matrix.
[06:16] Marcus Lee: We'll include an incident response runbook and primary/secondary contacts in the security pack.
[06:23] Diane Morales: For onboarding, what documentation and training do you provide?
[06:27] Ava Patel: Ava from CSM — we provide onboarding guides, integration SDKs, example prompts, observability setup (per-route dashboards), and a kickoff with SE for configuration. We also do a 1:1 with your ops team for the Dedicated or Private setup.
[06:40] Lena Ortiz: Instrumentation is key — we want per-route latency and token counts, also token-level cost breakout.
[06:45] Marcus Lee: Our Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll show a demo if useful.
[06:54] Tom Nguyen: Last legal item: export controls and data residency clauses — we need explicit assurance that data won't be moved out of region X.
[07:02] Sofia Chen: For Dedicated/Private we can lock region and disable cross-region failover. We'll propose explicit data residency language in the DPA.
[07:10] Diane Morales: Good. Let's recap action items and next steps.
[07:14] Sofia Chen: Recap: 1) Sofia to send pricing tiers and committed capacity worksheet by Monday (11/30). 2) Marcus to share benchmark plan, SLA samples, and security pack by Wednesday (12/2). 3) Tom to return MSA/DPA redlines with non-starters by Friday (12/3). 4) Lena to confirm data residency and KMS preference by 12/4. 5) Schedule pilot kickoff — we'll propose dates after we align on scope.
[07:39] Diane Morales: That works. We may push some of those dates depending on legal calendar but will try to keep to them.
[07:45] Raj Patel: One last question — are there any vendor attestation programs for healthcare compliance beyond SOC2?
[07:51] Marcus Lee: We have HIPAA-facing documentation and can provide a BAA for Covered Entities; additional attestation like HITRUST is not in our standard pack but we can discuss enterprise support paths.
[08:03] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[08:06] Sofia Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the materials and a proposed pilot plan.
[08:10] Tom Nguyen: Thanks, bye.

End of call.
